Originally I was looking for a splitter that would allow for my input devices to connect to both via usb. This switch does allow that, though not at the "same time." You do have to select one or the other via the switch.

Aside from its designed task, it does give you access to extra USB ports. There are 4 ports and only 2 are being used. It is very easy for me to reach across my desktop and plug in a device to charge, or plug in a thumb drive to save a file instead of reaching underneath the desk on my hands and knees. I love this product and the price is right. No need in my opinion to pay more.

EDIT: I have changed rating from 5 starts to 2 stars. The switch just died after 9 months of use. There is power going to both sides of the switch, but no data going back to the computer. I emailed customer service 2 times during the past week and have not gotten a response. Maybe they are off for Christmas? I don't now what they do in China. I have been happy with all the Ugreen products I have used and it's possible this may be a fluke. If the company continues to ignore my emails I will probably purchase a device from a different manufacturer. I am a little annoyed.

text_fidelity_a:
APEKX Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth 5.3: IPX7 Waterproof, Stereo Sound, Built-in Mic, Earbuds for Gym & Workouts, True Wireless Earphones (Black) I've had several different pairs of earbuds, all purchased from Amazon and none were name brands. So far, with the wrapping ear piece, this pair seems to stay on my ears much better than the buds that just pop into the ears. They paired easily to my iPhone and connect automatically each time I take them out of the case. The sound is decent or at least decent enough for me. I do not use these for just listening to music or videos, I have better over the ear headphones for that purpose. For me, I just use these for running, working out or maybe while working around the yard. For that purpose, the sound quality is pretty good. The only suggestion I have is remember to take the clear tape off the charging contacts; I did not realize it was there and my earbuds were not charging each time I put them back in the case. On the upside, I did learn that the battery life is excellent on these earbuds. I cannot say how long they actually lasted before I charged them, but I probably went on 5 or 6 runs before the first ear bud died. With the tape off the contacts, they do charge automatically each time they are placed back in their case. A nice feature is that the case can be charged either with a cord or by setting the case on a charging pad. The price was reasonable. I would recommend these wireless earbuds to anyone looking for a set. Since I cannot fully say how long they will last or how durable they are, I will reserve the 5th star until I have owned these for a while.

Updated 12May21: Ok, I really want to like earbuds, but I cannot. As many times as I have tried earbuds, they just always feel like they are coming out of my ears, even w/the ear wraps on these buds. Having to continuously re-seat the ear buds in my ears while running just doesn't make for a comfortable run. So, I went back to a pair of wired BT headphones; which sit in my ears much better.
text_fidelity_b: APEKX Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth 5.3: IPX7 Waterproof, Stereo Sound, Built-in Mic, Earbuds for Gym & Workouts, True Wireless Earphones (Black)

USB C Docking Station, UtechSmart 18in1 Quadruple Display Laptop Docking Station for MacBook Pro & Windows,Thunderbolt 3 Dock with SSD Enclosure 3HDMI VGA 100WPD 5USB-A SD/TF Slot 3.5mm RJ45 Everything about this dock is either confusing, misleading, or falsely. First of all, I’m not quite sure I see the point of having two hosts connect to it as I it does not seem to be a like a KVM switch in any way. For one, video output is dedicated to one or the other host depending on the port. There is no switch to toggle between hosts so USB devices seem to be shared? Honestly it’s not at all clear. The power supply also can only charge one host, I believe whichever is plugged in first. Since there is a single ethernet jack that both hosts share it also shares a single MAC ID. The only explanation for any of this seems to be to give a buyer some impression that it behaves like a KVM switch that allows you to share peripherals. In fact it’s not even clear what it does as the instructions are incomplete. Since I was unable to get a keyboard to work connected to it I presume can you either use the built-in keyboard or plug it directly into the laptop.

I honestly didn’t even fully unboxed this thing after reading the instructions and trying to make sense of them. Once I saw that video was not shared and that the resolution was appallingly low, all of the other issues were already moot. It is advertised as a thunderbolt 3 dock but it’s apparent that thunderbolt 3 support is quite limited and it’s really a USB-C dock. Seeing how the function of this device is very unclear a pure its existence only serves to fool customers like me into not having to use a KVM. Since the description and the instructions appear to be deliberately vague, it would seem this is the point. This also explains why it’s so much less expensive than a single host dock or a dual host KVM.

Back to Amazon with you!
text_fidelity_b: USB C Docking Station, UtechSmart 18in1 Quadruple Display Laptop Docking Station for MacBook Pro & Windows,Thunderbolt 3 Dock with SSD Enclosure 3HDMI VGA 100WPD 5USB-A SD/TF Slot 3.5mm RJ45

ProElife Ultra Thin Silicone Full Size Keyboard Cover Skin for 2017 2018 Apple iMac Magic Keyboard with Numeric Keypad MQ052LL/A A1843 US Layout (Item Folded in Packaging) (Ombre Blue) UPDATE (12/25/2021):

I have removed this skin (bought on January 27, 2020) for 3 reasons.
1. The keys were not so visible below the skin because it has become more translucent instead of remaining transparent.
2. The shift key on the left side was ripped from being used and from my fingernail, I would think. IOW, it's not so tough.
3. A sticky liquid has formed between my keyboard and the skin. I removed it with more than just wiping. No solvent has been used at any time. Perhaps the silicone reacted with the plastic keys. Nothing has ever been spilled on the keyboard. Still, I have a skin on the keyboard as protection against any liquid OR dust OR hair getting into my keyboard that I have been using since 2008 when it was new.

My replacement (Allinside) is now in place and I can once again see the keys.
The skin fits the keys such that it does NOT have to wrap around the edges of the keyboard.

UPDATE (7/14/2018): After one year I have to replace this keyboard skin because it is wearing out in several places, mainly the left side command key where there is a ¼ inch slit. When I have to type a long document / letter, I remove the skin so I can type faster on the aluminum keyboard because the keys require only a light touch. I have not switched to a BT keyboard because this one is so good, and the fact that it is wired is not a problem with a little tape to keep the cable out of the way when I slide the keyboard shelf in and out. The skin I received is transparent with nothing printed on any of the keys.

For those who have the wired Apple aluminum extended keyboard (with keypad), this product fits correctly to protect the keyboard from dust and spills. It is in use on my Mac Pro (early 2008). The description says for iMac, but it fits any of these keyboards of this style, not just the iMac keyboard.

It arrives folded, but that does not matter if it comes from a seller in the US who delivers it in a timely manner.

The keyboard cover does make it necessary to slow down the typing speed. That's not a real problem unless one is a touch typist or writer who spends a lot of time on the keyboard.
text_fidelity_b: ProElife Ultra Thin Silicone Full Size Keyboard Cover Skin for 2017 2018 Apple iMac Magic Keyboard with Numeric Keypad MQ052LL/A A1843 US Layout (Item Folded in Packaging) (Ombre Blue)

Headphone Adapter Converter Supports Audio and Charging for Motorola MotoZ, Letv ,2 in 1 USB-C to 3.5mm Audio Adapter, Nylon Braided 2 in 1 USB Type C Cable Fast Charge to 3.5mm Audio Jack(Black) This is a much easier alternative to the My K-cup option if you want to use your own coffee in a K-cup machine rather than the pre-packaged cups. Unlike the My K-cup you don't need to remove the inner cup of the machine to use this. It just drops right in, so you can switch between this and a regular k-cup without having to dismantle anything.

The kit is very complete. There are three cups, each a slightly different color (different shades of brown). The cups are decently made. The plastic sides are nice and thick; the o-ring on the cap is of good quality; and the metal mesh is firmly attached. My only quibble with the build quality is the hinge. It's plastic, and I don't have confidence that it will last a long time before breaking. It's not a big deal, since the cup will still work fine even with a broken hinge, so I'm not docking any points due to that potential problem.

I like that the water dispersion channel has slots all around it to ensure water gets sprayed in all directions inside the cup to keep the grounds uniformly wet. I also really like that the lip area has a slight indent to make it very easy to pop open the top with one hand.

It fit fine in my Cuisinart K-cup machine. The lid of the machine was just slightly raised compared with using a "real" k-cup, but it had zero impact on performance. I tried several different brews, all with good results. You will need to fiddle with the grind level to get the best coffee. Too fine of a grind and it gets over-extracted and bitter; too coarse and it's weak.

Cleaning a used cup is very easy. I pop open the top, hold it upside down in the compost pail, and whack it gently on the base with a wooden spoon. Nearly all the used grounds drop out, and what's left can be easily rinsed under running water. You can also just dump the contents into the disposal or garbage if you don't compost your grounds.

Another option is to use a mini filter in the cup. A package of them are included and, while they do make cleanup easier, I prefer to use just the cup without a filter.

The kit also includes a charcoal filter. I didn't use that, so I can't speak to its performance. It looks to be the same size as the filters used in the water intake of my Cuisinart K-cup machine, so I expect it would perform in a similar fashion.

This Smart Cup kit works well, is well-made/designed, and comes in a very complete kit. Having used the My K-cup version I can confidently say that this performs better and is easier to use. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Headphone Adapter Converter Supports Audio and Charging for Motorola MotoZ, Letv ,2 in 1 USB-C to 3.5mm Audio Adapter, Nylon Braided 2 in 1 USB Type C Cable Fast Charge to 3.5mm Audio Jack(Black)

The earbuds themselves are customizable, but bulky compared to the competition. I find them hard to get out of the container, hard to hold onto, and hard to wear. The noise cancellation and sound are both above average though. I like the charging light on the container. It communicates with color and flashes what the status of the product is, and isn't bright or hard to locate.

USB-C charging makes the base station charge up nice and fast. It holds the earbuds securely, and doesn't rattle or fall open. It's also a nice pocketable size and shape with no sharp corners, making the whole product especially portable. Controls are gesture, rather than button. I'm not a fan of this because I end up doing a lot of swiping and hoping. A click button interface, I can just click it the number of times I know will do what I need, and move on.

I've got a few Sony audio products that I use every day and am very happy with, but with earbuds, I'm sticking with jabra for now. It's a competitive market right now for earbuds. Lots of companies putting out new designs.
text_fidelity_b: Sony WF-1000XM4 Industry Leading Noise Canceling Truly Wireless Earbud Headphones with Alexa Built-in, Black

HP 1KF76AA#ABL OMEN by Wired Gaming Headset 800 (Black/Red) Bear in mind that as gaming headphones, the sound quality is not as suited for other applications like listening to music. Having said that, here's how the experience went:

Appearance: maybe this is some macho thing, but they are enormous and intense-looking in an almost exaggerated way. So if you're one of those people that likes huge flashy stuff or ostentatiously masculine-looking things, this is perfect? They're huge.

Comfort: Very comfy! The cup part is large and fits great, and the headband adjusts nicely to most average head sizes. The microphone is fully adjustable, making it work for anyone.

Sound blocking: pretty good! While it does not use noise-cancelling technology, the sheer size and generous build of the headphones allows for Very effective sound cancellation. I had my partner listen to something with her back to me so she could not see me, and with the volume turned up, I had to full on Scream for her to hear me.

Sound quality: Better for spoken word and voices, honestly. The sound is crisp and detailed, but it's also a little canned-sounding, with somewhat sharp, tinny trebles and less-than-intense bass. This does best in mid-range and capturing voices and sounds, and less so for actual music. Having said that, it is certainly better than cheap headphones for music, so it does have some versatility if you're not too picky.

Overall: These are pretty great! They even have an adapter that can be used by other devices that unites the audio input and output, which comes split for certain applications like computers or other gaming. (Meaning, theres a separate cable for the microphone and audio input, and they come with an adapter to have a single "female" connection that can work on phones or other single-plug devices using audio in/out.)

Cool!

text_fidelity_a: Sony MDREX38iP/BLK EX Earbud with iPod Remote Control - Black I purchased these earphones for use with my new 3G iPod Shuffle because I was very happy with the Sony earbuds I used with the 2G iPod Shuffle. While the sound quality is comparable, the Y-style design of the cord is terrible because this little thing called gravity gets in the way. The super-long cord is also not fun because I find myself constantly managing it to ensure it doesn't get tangled. In contrast, Sony's over-the-should "OFC neckchain" design in the previous version coupled with the modular approach they took to the cord - approx. 1 foot with an optional 3 foot extension - meant that I could clip the previous iPod on the inside of my coat and be unconstrained by a long cord. Ultimately, the whole idea of a remote that is integrated into the cord feels like a misfire to me. The 2G generation iPod Shuffle plus the older generation of Sony earbuds are far more functional and I'm going back for as long as my old Shuffle will hold out.

Vanguard TBH-100 Ball Head (Black) When I purchased my Dolica AX620B100 tripod, it was advertised as having a ball head. However, the ball head on that tripod only moves side to side, it doesn't fully rotate. Since most of my photography is outdoors in the landscape, it took a little doing to make sure my photographs were level even on bumpy ground.

This Vanguard ball head attachment fixes all of that. I have three tripods and one monopod in the house, and it attached easily to all of them. The ball head is easy to adjust and has an intuitive friction control lever which allows you to move the ball head just a little or a lot. I feel like I've got great control. However, it never gets fully floppy to where you could accidentally damage your camera, as with a ball head I tried in the store.

I also really liked the turning action of the quick release knob, it feels a lot more secure than the usual lever that I'm used to.

Overall, this is a great addition to my humble set of landscape photography and video equipment. It's easy to use, took me about two minutes to figure out and attach, and gives me much better functionality than I had previously.

text_fidelity_a:
Lowepro Passport Sling DSLR Camera Bag I was looking for a sling camera bag for ease of use when I am in action mode, e.g., hanging off the side of a jeep during safari, hanging over the railing of a boat while photographing breaching whales. I did not want the typical backpack or the shoulder bag (both of which I own) that would impede me from such movements and/or would need to be set down while I was shooting.

I like to leave my zoom lens on my camera. I attach a lens in the open as few times as possible for the obvious reasons, e.g., salt air, dust. I have a Nikon 200-500 lens attached to a D4 body. With that configuration, the camera/lens is 14.25" long, D4 body is 6" wide and lens at its widest is 5" and it fills this bag's length (including the unzipped 30% extra). That set up is also about 10-11 pounds of weight. However, in order to fit it . . . I had to remove the square cushioned "cube" that is affixed by velcro into one side of the bag. Once my cameras/lens was in the bag, there was about 3" of horizontal (lengthwise space) left and 3" of vertical space as well as small pockets of space around the camera/lens itself. I would not be able to fit my IPad. I could probably tuck my IPhone in somewhere. Extra batteries, battery charger and cords would be doubtful. One extra battery perhaps.

The zipper on the top can be zipped either way (which I like). There are cords on the zippers as well for easy grabbing. The "open" pockets on the outside are nice, and while they are 6" deep, there isn't much that has any value that I would store there . . . because the risk of it falling out would be too great. (At least for me . . . because I plan to sling the sling quite a bit). It is difficult to believe that the inside of this bag only has 2 very small pockets. Both pockets have flaps that velcro. One pocket is 4"d x 3"w and the other is 4"d x 2"w. While that seems like a lot . . . the pockets are sewn into the bag and some of that width is lost to the stitching. They are immediately adjacent to each other and immediately under the top zipper (not the most optimum place to be IMHO).

The strap is nice and sturdy and reminds me of my Nikon strap. What I also like is that instead of having the typical strap tightener (don't recall the technical term, but like a buckle), this strap has a cam lock buckle. It is a buckle clip that clips down with pressure on the strap. It will take you less time to adjust your strap, which might not be a big deal to some . . . if you don't adjust your strap very often. Loaded it down with approximately 12 pounds of equipment, slung it on my back and tested it by moving around for a while today . . . and it stayed put. Hopefully, it will do the same when in the field. Strap has 6" wide removable cushion that velcros into place. I will probably double that with another one to make it super comfy. I am 6'0" tall. With the strap over my left shoulder (and the bag sitting on my right hip) and the strap completely extended . . . the top of the bag (where it zips open), is approximately 25" vertically from my right shoulder.

Canvas feels heavyweight. It feels like it might be waxed (and therefore water resistant), but after a bit of due diligence, I cannot find anything that would confirm same. But, you could sling this over your shoulder under a rain jacket or poncho if necessary.

The color is just right for safari (bright colors, whites, greys and/or blacks are frowned upon). This is the main reason why I did not purchase the Passport II or III . . . no natural color choices.

I would describe myself as an intermediate amateur photographer and it has become my hobby in retirement. I live for nature action shots.

I am keeping this bag. I am going to cut off one side of the cushioned "cube" to make a cushioned "U". The open end of the "U" will face up. I will place the camera in the bag so that the cushioned U will cradle my large lens with my camera attached. While it doesn't hold as much as I would like . . . I liken it to a wristlet wallet. It holds exactly what I need at the time I need it. I will still have my camera backpack with me (to hold extra batteries, lenses and the like) and my hubby usually volunteers for carry duty - lucky me! I would like to have given it 5 stars . . . but I feel as though the design needs improvement (the II and III are about the same in size etc.). Unfortunately, this also seems to be the only true sling bag on the market. (My definition of sling is worn like a crossbody with the bag on your back instead of in front).

Look forward to breaking it in very soon.
text_fidelity_b: Lowepro Passport Sling DSLR Camera Bag

It caused one reboot on installing a lot of software over a slow Internet connection (it was during the upgrade of the software, and might have been caused by that) but it has been running flawlessly ever since.

It is stable, reliable, and quiet.

Don't let the speed be an issue here. Sony bullt at 5400 into the PS4 originally, so it will not need faster, and a faster drive could cause overheating. Two things to keep in mind when downloading the Sony firmware though. First, the folder names are case sensitive. PS4/UPDATE not ps4/update. If you are going to use this to upgrade the PS3, a thing to keep in mind when installing the system software is that the PS3 has trouble reading larger thumb drives. This nailed me when I tried a 120 gig drive. I had to roll back to an 8 gig, that did the trick.

For a laptop or netbook, I would favor a faster drive, but for the budget conscious, this one is excellent.
text_fidelity_b: WD Blue 1TB Mobile Hard Disk Drive - 5400 RPM SATA 6 Gb/s 9.5 MM 2.5 Inch - WD10JPVX

text_fidelity_a:
Linksys WiFi Extender, WiFi 6 Range Booster, Dual-Band Booster, Internet Repeater, 2,000 Sq. ft Coverage, Speeds up to (AX1800) 1.8Gbps - RE7310 You should know up front that this extender only works wirelessly with dual-band WiFi routers (routers with both 2.4GHz and 5GHz).

But it will work as a hard-wired range extender for single-band routers (2.4GHz) using an ethernet cable.

If you have a single band router like we do, it will not detect the wireless network or connect wirelessly. If our neighborhood is any indication, this extender won't work with most home routers. Out of the ten or so visible wireless networks in our area, the extender only detected one or two. The two it detected were two of the weaker signals, but I assume were dual band signals the extender would work with.

After several frustrating attempts to get it connected wirelessly, I spent about an hour with customer support before being informed of this limitation on the extender. The product listing says "compatible with all Wi-Fi routers," and it may be compatible with all routers if set up as a wired extender, but apparently it isn't compatible with all as a wirelessly connected extender. If you want wireless connection to your router, check your router's capability and make sure it is a dual-band router before ordering.

As I mentioned, I did get it set up as a wire-connected extender using an ethernet cable. And it works well for that. It puts a good strong WiFi signal all over our house and much of the yard. I'm giving it four stars for that.
text_fidelity_b: Linksys WiFi Extender, WiFi 6 Range Booster, Dual-Band Booster, Internet Repeater, 2,000 Sq. ft Coverage, Speeds up to (AX1800) 1.8Gbps - RE7310

Cable Matters DisplayPort to DVI Adapter (DP to DVI Adapter) My desktop computer has a built in graphics card on the motherboard and I added a graphics card for gaming. The graphics card has a DVI, VGA and DisplayPort outputs. I had two monitors hooked up, one to the DVI, and one to the VGA port. I had another monitor (actually a TV) which duplicated screen two using a splitter. But I wanted to use it as a third separate monitor.

I tried several things to make a third monitor work: a DVI to HDMI cable (not an active cable) didn't work - the computer never saw the third monitor. I also tried the built in graphics card on the motherboard, plugging in an HDMI cable to its port and connecting the TV. That didn't work. it seems only one graphics card can be enabled at a time; either the one on the motherboard, or the installed graphics card.

This worked. As soon as I plugged it in, going from the displayport on the graphics card to the HDMI cable, the computer saw & recognized the 3rd monitor. Now I have three separate monitors.
text_fidelity_b: Cable Matters DisplayPort to DVI Adapter (DP to DVI Adapter)

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra STONE Bluetooth Headset with Extreme-Noise Blocking (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I think this is a good electronic gadget. Actually, it made me upgrade my phone to one that uses Bluetooth. I was still using a cell phone that only lets you receive and make calls, and play a few games so I guess it was time to move forward technically speaking.

The sound is clear, I had my daughter answer the phone at home while I was driving and it worked marvelously. She could easily understand me and vice-versa. After I got home I put my cell phone on the kitchen table after calling my land-line and I walked outside of the house with the Jabra Stone only. I was surprised that I was still able to talk to my daughter from almost 100 feet away from my cell phone. As I walked down the driveway and into the street it finally lost connection. But, I know that at least within a few feet I don't need to always have my cell phone right with me.

The Jabra Stone worked just like the directions said it would but I still kept messing it up during the learning curve. I wish it was a little more secure around my ear and for those who like to tuck their long hair behind their ears (me) it's difficult to do that with the earpiece on. And I have to remember to untuck my hair before putting it on or it will not go on. But once you get the hair problem solved it's well hidden - I don't think anyone can see it while I wear it. Also, it only works for the right ear, at least as far as I can tell so I don't know if it can be modified some way to hook on the left ear. I tried to fit onto my left ear but couldn't figure out a way to do so. So, if you are deaf in your right ear I would check to make sure it could be changed somehow to fit the left ear.

It's small, convenient and functional. So much easier than trying to drive and hold a phone at the same time, but I rarely drive and yak on the phone anyway since it's so dangerous. I don't want to be distracted from driving. But when out shopping or doing something else on foot and I'm expecting an important call it's great to have my hands free to continue shopping as I yak.

The reason for 4 stars instead of 5 - kind of loose on my ear, and the charger doesn't hold a charge for very long. It's frequently plugged into the wall re-charging. But it's great that you can hook the charger to your shirt pocket (men will like that) so you can continue to receive calls all day long.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra STONE Bluetooth Headset with Extreme-Noise Blocking (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony Ultimate One Remote - Discontinued by Manufacturer I've had a love/hate relationship with Harmony for the past 10 years...but no more second chances.

Just like every Harmony I've ever owned, setup for this required a call to tech support. I'm fairly tech savvy, and this should be easy to set up, but it wasn't. And I know it wasn't me because it took tech support 30+ minutes and 7 syncs to make it function "properly". Yes, "properly" is in quotes because even at its best, it was unimpressive.

On my own using the software, syncing failed to load my activities into the remote. And again...it took tech support 7 syncs to make it work.

Even after it was working "properly", it was still frustrating to use:

1) When switching between TV and SMART TV, it would power the speaker bar on and off. Does Logitech not understand that TV and SMART TV are not 2 separate devices and if you are switching from one to the other the sound should be left on? With a remote this expensive I shouldn't have to dig out the speaker bar remote to turn it back on every time I switch activities.

2) Lack of physical buttons for numbers is annoying. Any time I need the number pad I have to swipe to unlock, then swipe to get to the number pad. Technology is supposed to make processes faster...not slower. And yes, I know I can turn off the lock feature...but then every time I grab the remote it does something I don't want, and that something usually requires time-consuming troubleshooting.

3) As I mentioned before, programming this remote is a nightmare (2+ hours) and even then it couldn't stand alone. I ran into problems only tech support could solve, and even then it took 30 minutes AFTER I had all the correct devices loaded. Please note that this was a simple configuration: Sony smart TV/Fios DVR/Samsung speaker bar. All less than 3 years old. After I returned this remote I bought a "learning" remote and endured programming every single button individually, and it still took a fraction of the time.

4) There is no POWER button. Only an OFF button. You turn things on by selecting an activity. And as stated before...switching to a new activity powers things off that a remote this expensive should understand should be left on. If you are going to have a single OFF button that powers down everything with an activity button that turns everything back on, you should have an ON button for each device so you can quickly turn on any device that for whatever reason doesn't turn on when you fire up the system with an ACTIVITY button. And again...having to do an initial swipe to get to the ACTIVITIES just to turn the system on is annoying. Why does Logitech insist on writing code that slows down the power-on process???

5) You cannot utilize the Harmony software without plugging in the device. Why??? When things aren't working correctly (which is often) we should be able to fire up the app just to review the settings. Then, when you do plug the remote in, you have to wait for the remote and your PC to establish communication. Don't software engineers understand that we HATE waiting for technology to do things? Especially when forced to plug in when we don't want to??? Speaking of plugging in, it is difficult with this remote. First off, there is a totally unnecessary door. That door gets in the way when you're trying to plug in, and plugging in is difficult enough already because the mini-USB port is deeply recessed inside the door. Do we really need to cause all this hassle just to hide a mini-USB port? C'mon Logitech...don't you guys own cell phones? Mini-USB doors are annoying and useless (which is why cell phones stopped using them). Try to keep up.

6) Tech support is only good for 90 days. Based on my experience with this remote and 2 previous Harmony remotes, this means that any changes I make to my very simple home entertainment system will not work, and I will not be able to get help to make them work.

A remote that costs well over $100 should assimilate my entertainment system like the Borg. It should be simple to set up, function extremely quickly/efficiently, and be highly intuitive. This device is just another example of technology that steals away hours of your your life that you will never get back.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony Ultimate One Remote - Discontinued by Manufacturer

This set is better than most headphones in the under $50 price range. Sound is clear and noise free. Volume is loud enough for earbuds, but not booming at full volume. Bass is kind of weak, though that is a common problem in this price range. 3 hour battery life is about average for this price range. Comparing $50 headphones to $100 headphones is not really fair, but if you do want to spend more money, most headphones will give you much better bass and richer overall sound quality. More expensive headphones also give me better battery life (usually at least 4 hours without any recharging). On the other hand, if I'm out running or riding on the subway, I'd rather use these $50 headphones instead of risk losing much more expensive headphones.

I am impressed by the build quality of these Soundcore headphones. They headphones feel solid. They are comfortable in my ears. The case is sleek and the recharging system works well. The buttons that control the headphones work easily and reliably. I do wish they used a modern USB-C charging system instead of the old-fashioned micro-USB.

Magellan Crossover 3.5-Inch Portable GPS Navigator OK, so I can't compare the performance of this GPS system to any other as this was the first time I've ever used or needed something like this. But I read a lot of reviews, and I do mean a lot of them, for a couple of weeks before making my decision and I'm pleased that for a first experience I purchased a Magellan Crossover.

Let me explain, I work in sales. I travel to a lot of large towns/ small cities in my territory that are in Arkansas. I had never been to these towns before. Apparently, the city leaders do not care if one can find their way around them because most of them have terrible city maps available and/or do not bother to put street signs up. This made it a challenge to find my customers even with a map.

So the idea of a GPS came to mind and I took the plunge. This little unit worked exactly the way I wanted for 2 days then stopped working half way through the second day. Not even pressing the reset button helped. (sigh) I called the people I purchased it from and they paid to have it Fed-Exed back to them for replacement. Apparently I got a defective model. Hey, it happens to all of us. So by the end of this week I'll have my replacement and will be ready to roll again.

This was a great time saver for me. I would get to a town, input the first address and it would get me to my first stop. When I was done there I would input the next address and it accurately got me to the next place I needed to be. It literally saved me a couple hours a day in wasted travel time by my not having to stop, get directions from a local (that were usually wrong) and repeating that process over and over.

The screen was bright and easy to read, the voice plenty loud enough. And the unit was easy learn to use. I gave it 5 stars for performance. I can't really fault the manufacturer for a faulty unit. Those things are hard to predict and usually are few and far between.

So, unless the next unit is also defective, at which time I will then have to reconsider and write a more negative review LOL, this little GPS unit is a great buy for a first time user.

[...].
text_fidelity_b: Magellan Crossover 3.5-Inch Portable GPS Navigator

I'm using this with a Kindle Fire 8.9. Pairing was quick and simple.

The connection to the stereo can be done via a single cable or using a two cable (L/R) setup. Cables for both options are included. I'm using the L/R option, and plugged the cables into the TAPE input on my stereo receiver.

The sound quality is excellent. It is very hard to tell the difference in quality when streaming audio via this receiver versus playing a CD on the receiver. Movie dialog was outstanding as well.

The fact that it does not require a battery is a plus and a minus. On the plus side, no need to worry about recharging or swapping batteries. On the down side, it was a bit of a problem for me to get the cables routed since the wall outlet near my stereo is not easily accessible. I wound up running a short extension cord so that I could plug in the receiver close enough to the stereo so that the L/R cables would reach.

As a bonus, it includes a USB port so you can use it to recharge your phone/tablet/etc.

That one minor issue aside, I'm very impressed with the performance of this product. Highly recommend.

text_fidelity_a:
CyberPower CP1350AVRLCD Intelligent LCD UPS System, DISCONTINUED * SEE NEW UPDATED MODEL CP1350AVRLCD3 * A UPS is one of those products you don't give much thought to until you are in a situation where you REALLY need it to work. The display on the Cyberpower is a great feature - tells you all sorts of useful info such as your battery status, run time, load level and others so you always know what's going on.

Nice footprint, puts out very little heat (compared to a Tripplite that this replaces which threw off a huge amount of heat - nice in the winter time, but not so nice in the summer), simple setup. My only complaint, and the reason it lost one star, is the spacing of the outlets. You have to use outlet extenders if you have the "wall wart" transformers. I have three of them (modem, router and external hard drive) - they all fit on the Tripplite since it offers widely spaced outlets, but couldn't fit them into the Cyberpower without extenders.

The other nit is the location of the power button. It's right on the face of the unit, and you have to be careful not to hit it accidentally. A better design would be to either locate it somewhere else or, better yet, put a safety lock on it so you can ensure you don't power down unless you truly want to do so.

Both are minor issues and can be easily worked around. I'm very pleased with the unit so far, and recommend it to anyone looking for a good UPS and a nice price.
text_fidelity_b: CyberPower CP1350AVRLCD Intelligent LCD UPS System, DISCONTINUED * SEE NEW UPDATED MODEL CP1350AVRLCD3 *

I have tried several other similar devices and they all had serious problems, while this provides 87W of power, dual display support (DisplayPort 1.2), both an analogue and digital audio (TOSLINK) device, SD card reader, and extra 5 Gbps Thunderbolt 3/USB-C and USB 3.0 ports.

Regarding the 1 star reviews, with the exception of the person with the defective unit, I am almost positive the problems people have been having are because of their cables. Most people don't realize that the white USB-B cable that comes with their MacBook (which they probably just use for power) is Thunderbolt 2 and will NOT support Thunderbolt 3 devices! To connect your computer to the dock, use the cable they provide. If you need a longer cable, be sure to buy an actual Thunderbolt 3 cable that is less than 2 meters long. As for your display cables, it is critical the cable is DisplayPort 1.2. I also connected the second monitor to the Thunderbolt 3 port that converted to DisplayPort 1.2 (I just got the Amazon Basics brand and it works as it should. I have used this on both my 2017 and 2019 MacBooks and they both work flawlessly. Its so nice to just have one cable to plug and unplug for all devices!

Kindle Paperwhite, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi [Previous Generation] I bought for my mother as a mother's day gift. I also bought a Vera Bradley cover and a $50 Amazon GC to go with it. My mom is not the gadget type. No matter how many times I explain how to change TV setting from the Playstation to the cable box, which for our TV is a one button push, she just cannot do it. So, getting a Kindle was a stretch, however, I wanted her to have the ability to travel without taking a lot of books with her because my mom is also that mom who over packs and has too much stuff, which inevitably means she loses something.

So, the Kindle only gets use when she travel, but she has figured it out somewhat. She can't quite figure out how to purchase books or how to change the settings, which she just gets me to do it for her, but it has gotten a lot of use because she does take it with her instead of a bunch of books. In my use of this Kindle, I find it somewhat clumsy, slow, and some of the icons are not self explanatory and takes a few tries going back and forth. What I do like is that the screen is the exact size of a paperback book, there is no glare whatsoever, which is a problem I have with my iPad, and the light in the screen is perfect for reading at night without a lamp on. The ability to have all of Amazon's e-books at your fingertips is nice if you have a Wi-Fi connection. I don't see a reason to get the 3G as this is just a Kindle for reading only, thus, I and my mother can wait til a Wi-Fi connection is available to download another book if need be. However, you can download multiple books at a time so if you just can't stand not having something to do for 20-30 mins, I would suggest downloading more than one.

Battery life is out of control! I have never seen this go below 50% even after hours of use. One downside is that the plug to charge it is not included so you will have to also pay for that as well. It is also very lightweight, and if you have a little case it's like holding an actual paperback, unlike an iPad which is much heavier and cumbersome to read e-books on.

However, overall, I'm old school. I like paper books. The smell, the ability to write notes and see those notes on the margins, the feel of the paper between my fingers. I can go my references quicker and don't have to worry about running out of memory space because my books stay on a shelf until I need them. So, I recommend this for travel only for the sake making room in your carryon. It is easy to use once you learn all the little quirks. Otherwise, the geek/nerd in me just always goes back to actual black and white.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Paperwhite, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi [Previous Generation]

Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White Great price and fun to play with. If you're interested in smart home technology this is a great place to start since it's easy to use and connect to other devices down the road. I bought several as Christmas gifts and when people figured out how to use it they loved it. The built in speaker is ok, I knew it wasn't as good as the more expensive Echo so I wasn't disappointed. If you already have a Bluetooth speaker or sound quality isn't a huge factor for you out of the box then you can't beat the price. I don't have any issues hearing Alexa's responses with the built in speaker, but when I want to listen to music I just connect my Bluetooth speaker (very easy to do) and can move it around the house with no problems. We have a dot on each floor of our house (2 stories) that are located in the most used areas. I keep a Bluetooth speaker in our bedroom and use the Alexa remote to interact with the Dot in our tv room since she can't hear me as well. This allows you to still connect to, and hear Alexa, without having to yell and strain to hear her.

The shopping list and to do list feature I really like since I'm horrible at writing down what we need around the house before I go shopping. I just tell her what to add to my list as I notice it, and it instantly shows up in the Alexa app which I can open when I get to the store and add/delete items. I also love these features to capture random things I want to research later like book titles, tv shows, serial numbers for parts etc that I might forget if I don't have it written down somewhere.

The only reason I didn't give the dot 5 stars is because most of the skills that are available right now leave a lot to be desired. I'm sure down the road this will improve but there isn't a lot to choose from right now that has a lot of practical use. Like a lot of people I would prefer Alexa be able to answer questions based on a Google search rather than having to enable skills for different things. If I want to know what flu symptons are she doesn't understand what I'm asking. But when you factor in everything she can do, and what she can connect with, then the dot is definitely still worth purchasing based on the price.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White

text_fidelity_a:
Lifeproof NüüD Series Ipad Air 2 Waterproof Case - Retail Packaging - Black 4.5 stars!

This case is pretty amazing! It is slim, VERY lightweight, and almost completely waterproof. I even did the submerging test, and much to my surprise, it had no leakage whatsoever. Very cool. Below are some details:

Protection: 4.5 stars
I can't help it. I love protecting the screen, and this doesn't do that. I had to take half a star off. Other than that, the body is VERY safe in this device, not just from drops, but from liquids and most day-to-day nonsense. But in a bag, where the face might get scratched? meh... not so much! It was also a little unclear if you could apply a screen protector and still keep all the benefits like it being water-proof.

On that note--the waterproofing is impressive. The clever design uses a tight rubber seal around the areas where water might penetrate, allowing your ipad to still be exposed where it is safe (the screen). It even has a special extension that allows you to use the headphone jack. VERY cool.

Functionality: 4.5 stars
You can use the charging port and heaphone jack fine, but the speakers don't sound so great with this. (Completely understandable, and it's just a trade-off you have to make if you plan on making a mess on your pretty toy ;-) This is why we can't have nice things, am I right?)

Design: 5 stars
The concept and execution are brilliant, combining functionality with durability, practicality with aesthetics. While putting it on and taking it off is an ordeal, the flip side of that is the fact it won't fail you. This case is dependable. Best of all, unlike some similar super-strong cases, this one is low-profile and lightweight--not the clunky thing you would expect at all.

EXCELLENT
text_fidelity_b: Lifeproof NüüD Series Ipad Air 2 Waterproof Case - Retail Packaging - Black

Soundcore by Anker Life A2 NC Multi-Mode Noise Cancelling Wireless Earbuds, ANC Bluetooth Earbuds with 6-Mic Clear Calls, 35-Hr Playtime, and Deep Bass, Fast Charging, Transparency, and App The first couple of generations of Soundcore headphones were pretty mediocre. I'm glad the company keep improving their products. This year's models are really good for the price.

I got the Life A2 model. For $80, these earbuds come with features that I usually see on earbuds that cost more than $100 like equalization, noise cancellation, and upgradable firmware. These features all work great. I especially like the equalization that noticeably improves sound clarity.

Overall, the sound quality is great for earbuds that cost less than $100. Bass is not boomy, but great if you like a more natural sound. Stereo separation is excellent. Clarity at the higher frequencies is excellent when I set the equalizer to type of music that I'm listening too. Volume is better than average for true wireless earbuds.

These earbuds are on the larger side, but they don't stick out of my ears too much, so I don't constantly knock them out like I do with Apple-style earbuds. They are comfortable and secure enough in my ears.

I'm using an Android smartphone and the earbuds pair easily with my phone. Bluetooth connection has been solid. The Soundcore Android app is necessary to manage the equalizer and upgrade the firmware and both features work great. The app also shows your battery levels. Unfortunately, the app does spam me occasionally with unrelated Anker product announcements. I wish they wouldn't do that. Anker spams me enough by email.
text_fidelity_b: Soundcore by Anker Life A2 NC Multi-Mode Noise Cancelling Wireless Earbuds, ANC Bluetooth Earbuds with 6-Mic Clear Calls, 35-Hr Playtime, and Deep Bass, Fast Charging, Transparency, and App

text_fidelity_a:
Winegard HD8200U Platinum VHF/UHF HDTV Antenna (65 Miles+, Digital, 4K Ultra High-Def Ready) First, be aware this beast is more than 14 feet long and about 9 feet wide when unfolded and assembled. It does move in the wind. It doesn't weigh that much, but with so many elements forming such a large device it becomes a sail.

I mounted it on a 10' length of 1-1/4" electrical conduit held to a tall garage wall using [[ASIN:B001RCMEEA Channel Master CM-9025 3-Inch Heavy-Duty Wall Mount for TV Antenna Masts]]. The antenna is about 23 feet in the air.

The HD8200U has a very high-gain, directional Yagi UHF antenna on the front and a full VHF antenna on the rear. I really don't think I need the VHF section and may retire this antenna and opt for a more compact UHF Yagi if the high winds we occasionally experience cause trouble. After assembly, the two sections feed into an electronics box using 1/8" aluminum rods from each section. You then mechanically attach a top plate to the box that connects to all four aluminum leads. The coax connector is in this top plate. A weather boot is supplied to seal the connection.

The HD8200U does bring in the signal like a champ. My stations are at least 19 miles and 68 miles away. It's very directional. If I aimed 30 degrees off, I got zero channels. Check where your stations are broadcast from using www.antennaweb.org (antennaweb dot org) which provides distance and direction in degrees from magnetic north using your zip code. Very handy.
text_fidelity_b: Winegard HD8200U Platinum VHF/UHF HDTV Antenna (65 Miles+, Digital, 4K Ultra High-Def Ready)

I have tried the different options that come with them to get a better fit and stay in my ear tighter to no avail.

For outdoor activity, I cannot wear these. They fall out of my ear and I lose them. However, indoors I love the Alexa integration. If they could make them in a way they stay in my ear, they would be perfect. Last night, one fell out and went into the garbage disposer. Luckily, it was not on and water wasn't running or it would have been gone.

As they work loose quickly, sound quality and volume diminishes. They do have good bass response when tightly fitted in your ear. If I am sitting still listening to music or an audio book, they work great. As I start to move around, they loosen up and sound poor and are at risk of falling out.

Overall, I do have a use for them. I love the ability to use Alexa. I wish they could do Alexa independent of a mobile device via wi-fi, which they cannot. I love the ability to recharge them from the case when traveling. The case is hard shell and very protective of the earbuds. The case is probably the best part of the product.

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic SC-BTT195 Energy Star 5.1-Channel 1000-Watt Full HD 3D Blu-Ray Home Theater System with Tall Boy Speakers Good sound for the money and does what I expected. Skip to the summation if you are looking for reasons not to purchase.

Might be a better choice especially if you own a Panasonic TV as the set up is designed for a Panasonic product line. I had to use their support call service a few times and as most companies today, some are very good and can understand and help, but most will read a prewritten script and hope they hit on the problem you are experiencing. Cons: Had to go buy after market speaker wires due to the lack of length that comes with the system and splice the wires to place the rear speakers. Also had to buy an audio connector to allow the system to produce TV sound. This really ticked me off and Panasonic should really step up and correct these issues. The system also needs to modernize and add another HDMI connection ( and the cable ...really? ) to allow for a cleaner install. Another con is the system will not produce sound while watching the Internet based VUDU movie channel. Panasonic wanted me to buy another movie and call them to "try" some fixes while the movie played! It does work with my cable provided paid movie service. The system would also not work with my top of the line wireless router and had to buy a cable and run wires to their system. One must also buy another adapter ( Dingle) to receive wireless signals that may or may not work or a connecting cable. Check to see see the distance from your router to the system and if it is physically possible to fish the wire to the sound system from the router before you buy the cable.

Summation: "You get what you pay for". If you can splice wires and figure out how to add cables to make TV audio work and the internet work then it's ok. You will need to spend more money on items that should be included from Panasonic and it is best to own a newer Panasonic TV for easier installation. Panasonic kind of ruined what should be a great experience by cutting corners to save money on wire and connections. Panasonic should provide more installation on information "needs" as part of their product description if they aren't not going to provide long enough speaker wire, HDMI connectors and inputs,or audio cables,or internet Dingle or cable.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic SC-BTT195 Energy Star 5.1-Channel 1000-Watt Full HD 3D Blu-Ray Home Theater System with Tall Boy Speakers

text_fidelity_a: Amazon Basics SDHC Class 4 16GB Secure Digital Card the plus to this card is obvious--it has a large capacity.  The con is that it is a little slow in picture-taking.  Depending on what you're looking for, you may be happy or dissatisfied. I used it in a Kodak flip-style camcorder/still picture taker and I liked the fact that I didn't have to worry about filling up the card.  I recorded at 720 and it did fine in the recording and in the downloading of the video--I really didn't notice any speed issues.  Picture-taking was a different story; there was a noticeable lag in taking still photos. I wouldn't dismiss this card for that reason, however, unless a difference of a second or so will matter to you.  Most of my still picture taking on vacation is done with a larger point and shoot Canon IS, so the lag time with the little camera didn't matter much to me as I either used it mostly for video as mentioned or took stills of landscape or posed photos.  To be honest, I prefer not to use such a large capacity card for photos anyway as I have a fear of something going wrong with the card and losing hundreds of photos as opposed to a few videos.  So I'm happy to keep this in the little compact video camera and snap the occasional slow photo. I wouldn't put it in my Canon for the above reason and also because the photos I take with that I'd be more concerned about the sluggish picture-taking.  Be selective about how you use it, and I think you'll be more than satisfied
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics SDHC Class 4 16GB Secure Digital Card

Kindle Fire HDX 7", HDX Display, Wi-Fi and 4G LTE, 16 GB - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation - 3rd) I update to the latest Kindle every year. The HDX 7" is great with Wi-Fi. I like the 64 GB and quad core processor. The dual band wi-fi can use more power than my Internet can really deliver. I will probably have to update my whole Internet package. When I use the wi-fi to do downloads, everything on my wi-fi slows to a crawl and my Internet movies on Amazon and home computer freeze till it is done. I think my phone company only offers 100 Mbps with my current package. This kindle is powerful and takes over my whole Wi-Fi service.
The power adapter is a little different this year and goes in at an angle (thought it didn't fit). The adapter comes with the Kindle.
I will be keeping my old Kindle Fire HD, because I still enjoy it and some of the old apps I am not tired of yet (not compatible to HDX). I will be able to upload more of my pdf's to this newer Kindle, because pdf's use a lot more space. Also I can download more TV shows and movies, since I live in the Amazon ecosystem.
I like the clock on the screen is back. When I open the Kindle cover, the clock is in the corner with the date. That was not on the HD, but was on the first Fire (it was bigger).
I like the offers, because it is important to me what else is available. The screen is beautiful as always. I did have to make some adjustments to brightness (using settings) and the books (using view) I am reading. Actually for us older folks, brighter is better.
The sound is nice. I was watching PBS channel out in my yard and my neighbors could hear it. The PBS channel app was not something I was aware of before, but loving it now (even with my Internet service).
The HDX is smaller than the HD 7", but the screen is still the same size.
The camera on the 7"HDX is better than the HD. I really like it, because it comes with its own app, and I don't have to download a free app like last year. The one on my 7" HD has problems but was free.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire HDX 7", HDX Display, Wi-Fi and 4G LTE, 16 GB - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation - 3rd)

Sleep Headphones, Lavince Bluetooth Sleeping Headphones Headband Soft Elastic Bluetooth Headband,Cool Tech Gadgets Sleeping Christmas Valentine's Day Birthday Gifts for Women&Men I am dealing with what they call cervical tinnitus. During a routine dental procedure the doctor damaged my cervical spine muscles and the muscles at the base of my skull. So the damage muscles are manifesting noises through my neck and up to my ears. It used to be a 10 out of 10 but I’m down to about 3 out of 10. But that high whine every night absolutely precludes good sleep.

I was so excited to get this product. The set up was easy and I fell asleep right away… But about 3 hours later I awoke to electronic blow back noises. I woke up in distress because I thought it had actually made the tinnitus volume in my ear louder. But once I turned it off… It was evident the blow back noise was coming from the speaker itself. Thank God.

Cervical tinnitus vs. hearing loss or ear damage tinnitus works in different ways … and I am certain this product works for many people…I am just posting my individual experience. I’m returning it and I pulled the trigger for the $99 pillow speaker which is the size of an iPad which is placed between your pillowcase and your pillow.
text_fidelity_b: Sleep Headphones, Lavince Bluetooth Sleeping Headphones Headband Soft Elastic Bluetooth Headband,Cool Tech Gadgets Sleeping Christmas Valentine's Day Birthday Gifts for Women&Men

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra Elite 7 Active True Wireless— Bluetooth Sports Earbuds Shake Grip for Secure in-Ear Fit — Ultimate Workout Earbuds, Adjustable Active Noise Cancellation, Fast Charging — Navy Whoever designed the packaging for this had some fun with it. Opening it all is an interesting experience, in a good way. On the box, it says "thoughtfully designed, purposely engineered, expertly built" I think for the most part, they live up to it. Something tells me they pay their product designers well.

As usual for earbuds, they're hard to pry out of the magnetic case. The case does have a charging light on the front. It's so tiny, you probably won't see it until you plug it in. It's bright despite being the size of a grain of sand. Easy to see, which is nice. Easy to cover if it's by your bed. The case is small, smooth, and well built. More pocket size than most such charging cases.

I tried on the earbuds and the fit is ideal for me, and I've tried about seven brands. As soon as I put them in, they started giving me instructions on how to pair them.

I was irritated to find that the instructions tell me to install an app to get further instructions and functionality. This is typically where things fail, and I was primarily wanting these for a Windows tablet, not my phone, but I gave it a shot. The app does indeed give further instructions on how to use them, and also updated the firmware with no fuss the second time I opened it, complete with flashing purple LED on the case. The app also has a bunch of adjustments to the level of noise cancellation, equalizers, many soundscapes, like rain and pink noise, that work well with the cancellation to block out the world. The button functions can also be rearranged, which is nice because every brand seems to be different, and it's nice to be able to switch it to something personally intuitive.

I ended up connecting them to both my tablet and my phone, and now when I put them on, they say, "two devices connected" If I'm playing audio on my tablet, and then pause it and play audio on my phone, it seamlessly plays whichever is running, though not both at once. I like that I should be able to listen to my tablet and then take an incoming call. I'm not an audiophile, but the sound quality seems excellent to me. I've tried a couple expensive brands with noise cancellation, and it's interesting. It doesn't remove background noise very effectively, but it does a bit. I think it's more that when it's turned off, they use the mic to pump in outside audio so it's almost like you aren't wearing them. Neither mode is especially effective, so I wouldn't buy them for that specifically, but It's a small benefit. It's best suited for making your audio your focus or your situational awareness your focus.

I tried them on a call and it went well. My first time using earbuds for a phone call, and I have no complaints.

Definitely my new favorite earbuds, and I've got pricier ones. So far price has had little impact on my earbud opinions, mostly because design is still so much more variable and important than quality. I've only got two notable criticisms. One, every set I try is harder than the last to pry out of the case. Magnets are great. So is a sleek look to everything. Give us a divot in the case where we can get a finger under the edge. The other problem is range. Range is average, but when I tried walking out of range, instead of announcing the problem and handling it, they just cut out and turned off. I had to actually put them back in the case before they would go back to playing.

Overall, even with a few minor quibbles, these have become my new favorite earbuds, after having about seven (from good brands) in my family's stash to try. They fit well, audio quality is very good, the app actually functions and they are just a very solid, comfortable offering.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Elite 7 Active True Wireless— Bluetooth Sports Earbuds Shake Grip for Secure in-Ear Fit — Ultimate Workout Earbuds, Adjustable Active Noise Cancellation, Fast Charging — Navy

After googling, I found that the only way to get past this was to use Diskpart and Clean the drive--that meant wiping out everything on the drive. So using Diskpart again, I used the command, Create Partition Primary. At this point, Diskpart couldn't do anything else. It would not create a volume to format, so I had to use Disk Management to create the volume and format it to exFat. I should state that the drive was recognized by my computer internally when it was connected to a Sata port, but once it was put into the Sabrent, it's drive information was changed and made unusable until I performed the procedure above. Not sure why this happened, maybe because it's a SSHD, but I kinda doubt it since I had no problems with the drive when connected to a Sata Port.
text_fidelity_b: SABRENT USB 3.0 Tool Free Enclosure for 2.5” and 3.5” Internal SATA Hard Drives (EC-KSL3)

Samsung Galaxy NX EK-GN120ZKAXAR Galaxy Wireless Smart Android 4G Camera 20.3MP Mirrorless Digital Camera with 4.8-Inch LCD with 18-55mm OIS Lens (Black) Just opening the box is a joy, making this a great gift. Instead of the usual plastic and white or brown packing, all is in a beautifully designed chic black, with every item showcased to perfection.
Easy set up, right out of the box. I bought the [[ASIN:B00C7EPVHY Samsung Galaxy Camera with Android Jelly Bean v4.2 OS, 16.3MP CMOS with 21x Optical Zoom and 4.8" Touch Screen LCD (WiFi - White)]]a few months ago (also a great camera if you don't want to mess with a cell service for your camera) so it took no time at all, but even if you're an android newbie, it's still simple and straightforward. The Samsung website has some terrific videos showing various features. After an initial get-to-know-ya with this camera, check out more cool things you can do. Also, I myself find it helpful in the beginning to download the PDF of the manual and print off parts I want. The whole manual is over 200 pages, so I just print off what I need.

And even if you're relatively new to photography you'll feel like a pro with an easy to change lens. And about the lens, WOW! Looking at this camera? Get the model that includes the lens! More about the lens later...I could not be more excited!

The Optical Image Stabilizer in the 18-55mm lens offers clear, sharp images. The NX System lens incorporates i-Function Technology which lets you control the camera from the lens itself. It provides one step control of the shutter speed.
The AF (Auto Focus) is fast at 0.17 (!!!) seconds so it easily catches up to your next shot.
Recently, I was photographing an awards ceremony. The 'money shot', of course, was the transfer of the award. My darn camera took so long to autofocus from the previous shot, I missed it. Got a second before, a second after. That will never happen again.
And this is really cool...put the viewfinder up to your eye, and the touchscreen is disabled so your face isn't interfere with the screen icons.

The GPS tracker enables photographers to capture their exact geographical location in real time.

I'm already picking out the goodies to add to this camera. Samsung has a 10mm Fisheye lens, a 20mm pancake lens for taking great landscapes and an 18-200mm zoom...jeez, too many to mention that can be purchased separately. There are a lot of NX cases on eBay, if you want the 'real' one, when I looked, it was cheaper via Amazon versus the Samsung website.
You can also get external flash, remote switch, microphone.

This is THE camera, and the future of all cameras. It's easy enough for a budding photographer, slick enough for the pro.

Any other questions or anything you WISH this review had, just click the 'comment' button below and I'll do whatever I can to help, be it a video, research, whatever. I love it and am happy to share whatever I can so that you can decide if it's right for you.

UPDATE EDIT 3/4/14: The features and options never seem to end on this camera! It can get complicated, but thankfully Samsung has a dedicated support line for it. I've called twice with questions, never had to wait too long. Because this product is so new, if they don't know what youre talking about, ask to be switched to 'professional camera equipment' NOT 'digital camera'.
I feel like there are no stupid questions, only stupid answers, so I admit I asked some stupid questions. They were explained with enough information that I could look up and research the rest.
Since I am NOT a lifelong camera person, some features that would be 101 to others were new to me. And I'm so glad I had the Galaxy with Android Jelly Bean v4.2 OS, 16.3MP first.
The more I peek into what it can do, the more excited I am. One thing I should clarify about my review...I say it is fine for a budding photographer, and it is, but if you just want something to take photos or movies that is point and shoot, you won't be taking advantage of it's full potential. This is a camera for geeks and tech junkies! If you are a newbie, but have the DESIRE, this can be a first pro camera.
There is nothing else like this out there right now.

Someone asked about a 'zoom button'. Like any professional camera, you zoom with the lens, you WANT to zoom with the lens. Part of what is cutting edge about this camera is the way the lens 'talks' to the camera. The information about the functionality of the lens is sent to the body of the camera, so that any options that you have to control the lens shows up on the screen. Each additional lens you may choose to add has different functionality...screen options CHANGE with each lens because the camera KNOWS which lens is on. This is HUGE!
NEVER has this been done before, and I believe it will change the art of photography.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy NX EK-GN120ZKAXAR Galaxy Wireless Smart Android 4G Camera 20.3MP Mirrorless Digital Camera with 4.8-Inch LCD with 18-55mm OIS Lens (Black)

Microsoft Wired Keyboard 600 (Black). Wired Keyboard for Gaming Experience. USB Connectivity. Spill Resistant Design. I bought this keyboard as a replacement for the original one came with my HP computer which is a USB wireless. I liked the original one but it can't be used with rechargeable AA for a long time. I had to keep recharging constantly. And I didn't like the idea of wasting throw away batteries.
This new keyboard is just as compact and light as the original, it's a minimalist's dream. Key stroke is very quiet and requires very short stroke kind of like using a notepad keyboard. Plug & play operation is extremely trouble free, you'll need no instruction at all. Some of the photos I have seen showing PS2(old type connection) adaptor included but mine didn't include it, which wasn't an issue for me. There's a special key for "calc" but I didn't have a problem starting it in a couple of key strokes, so it's not a big advantage. Another feature is its "spill-resistant design". It's nothing more than a several slits under the keyboard. If you spill water, it may help drying quicker, for anything else, you'll have a hard time getting it clean, probably never completely like any other keyboard.
Over all, I like everything about this keyboard with no negative opinion. Only thing I don't know about it is its durability but from the way I feel, it seems well made and will last for a long time.
The photo showing on this page is misleading. It comes with keyboard only without a mouse.

text_fidelity_a:
VIZIO Sound Bar for TV, 28” 2.1 Surround Sound System for TV with Wireless Subwoofer and Bluetooth, Channel Home Theater Sound Bar – Remote SB2821-D6 The first delivery had subwoofer that was dead on arrival. No power.

They sent a replacement. It works great. Music streaming from my phone or computer by bluetooth sounds great. Better than my Bose.

If you want instruction on how to operate this thing properly look at the copied review below. This was helpful.

One other or two were somewhat helpful.

The instructions they put in the package gets the thing on but doesn't tell you how to operate it.

FYI:

"Please handle this unit with care when taking it out of the box. The sub-woofer in particular, which has the speaker cone located on the bottom of the sub-woofer. If you grab it from the bottom, you could damage it very easily. When set up properly, I found this Sound Bar to have very good sound. However it did take me awhile to reach this state. Because like most men, I know everything, I skipped through the instructions, plugged in the sound bar and was extremely disappointed in the quality of the sound. Here are a few tips to make things easier. If you're doing a horizontal installation in front of the TV at ear level, the sound button the the bar should be located on top, and the small lights that show volume level, etc., should be located on the left when facing your TV. That way the speakers are facing you. Also, I had a difficult time finding the audio settings on my TV to turn off the internal speakers and use the external speakers. Naturally I thought, heck just turn down the volume on the TV speakers to zero and it should be the same thing. Wrong !! You have to find and turn on the external speakers, and turn off the internal speakers for this sound bar to work properly. The sound bar does come with a remote, which is an absolute necessity no matter which sound bar you order. Read the instruction manual carefully, as you have to use the 'previous" and "next" buttons to adjust the Sub-woofer, Bass and Treble settings. Since I know everything, I naturally assumed the volume up and down buttons would adjust these settings. Wrong !! Also, there are buttons to enable TruVolume, and TruSurround HD, but the manual doesn't clarify exactly when to use these settings or what they actually do. I suggest trying both settings and see if you notice any difference in sound quality. I've read a few complaints about the bass not being that strong, but I found it to be excellent. I wonder if these users had the sub-woofer in the correct location, and if they figured out how to raise the sub-woofer level using the remote, and if the sub-woofer stopped working and needed to be "re-linked". I had to re-link mine, and although the instructions could be better, got the sub-woofer working properly in a few minutes. With the sub-woofer is turned on, located in the right area, and adjusted with the remote, you should be very happy with the results. Why only 4 stars for this product? First, the instruction manual could have been more informative about the settings on the remote, and second the ergonomics of the remote are in my opinion very bad. The volume adjustment in particular is usually an up and down toggle on every remote I ever used, but not on this one. The technical designer genius of this remote decided to put a big square "enter/play/pause button between the up and down volume adjustment buttons. Hence adjusting the volume by feel is the worst of any remote I've ever had. That being said, once set up properly, you should be extremely happy with the sound quality of this sound bar."
text_fidelity_b: VIZIO Sound Bar for TV, 28” 2.1 Surround Sound System for TV with Wireless Subwoofer and Bluetooth, Channel Home Theater Sound Bar – Remote SB2821-D6

But, they could never sound as good as a nice set of external speakers.

I watch a lot of videos and listen to music through my laptop and was always left wanting for better sound. I ordered this set of Nylavee speakers based on a recommendation from a 'gamer' friend.

Being a gamer, a lot of his experience is based on the light show. I got to watch and listen as he went through some multi-player war games and was really impressed with the quality of the sound coming from his speakers. I'm not a gamer. I have only one nit to pick at. The speaker's faces should be mirror images of each other, not duplicate. The way they are now, it looks like two left speakers, instead of a left and right. This is minor. But, still bugs me.

Otherwise, this is a really good set of computer speakers for the money and I am very comfortable with giving these Nylavee speakers five stars.

Then, there was the added aggravation of losing local channels when the "free" local network and the satellite provider came to stalemates over contract negotiations and the networks blocked their "free" channels to coerce the satellite provider into paying more.  I decided to put up an antenna to get the "free" local channels. We are about 30 miles from the TV towers of the major local channels in this area and we have lots of trees. Mounted on the corner eave of the house and pointed in the general direction of the towers, this picked up the signals to all channels. Where I get 10 local channels on the satellite, with the antenna I get all of those plus 10 extra digital channels broadcast by some of the local networks.

Samsung BD-H5900 3D Blu-Ray Disc Player (2014 Model) Packaging--very minimal, which is nice. Box was just enough to fit the machine safely and snugly--no over packaging

Set up--lightning fast. Pop two (included) batteries in the remote, attach to TV, plug in, choose a language, connect to home wi-fi and ready to go in two minutes at the most. Check for software upgrade, there is one, download--all done in another minute.

Apps: Seems to be a lot of back and forth on Amazon Prime. Mine definitely does not support. These are the apps from the newest software update (June 20th, 2014)
hulu plus,
VUDU
Youube
Netflix
Opera TV store
Flixster
CinemaNow
Rhapsody
Picasa
AccuWEather
Twitter
Pandora
Target
Internet TV--horrible interface
Flickr

To be honest, I wouldn't use most of these, so I'm not all that impressed with the Apps, though certainly they have the most needed on one in Netflix. But as I have Amazon Prime, I'm sticking with our DVD player that allows me to access it (I also have an Apple TV, which is why these apps don't do much for me). I'll also say some of these apps had terrible interfaces (yes, I'm looking at you Internet TV)

Build quality: I don't know if it really matters at all with a DVD player--I mean, it's going to sit up there and not really get any abuse I assume. But it does feel a bit light, not all that solid. If it were something portable and had that feel, I'd have some concerns. Not so much with this kind of device. It has a relatively small footprint.

I had not problem with several DVDs, both blu-ray and regular. Menu movement was fast, start-up time no different from any others I've used--not noticeably better or worse. Picture was fine, again, no better or worse than others I've sued (Sony, JVC)

screen is a bit too bright. Personally, I'd find it annoying, but others may not notice.

It's not a bad player at all, does most of what it needs to OK, but I definitely prefer our Sony for its larger app features and dimmer screen (it also feels more sturdy).

I can't think of a rougher stress test on performance, and it meets the challenge easily. It's rugged, reliable, and comes with built in drive encryption for your protection. I can read and write files with no problem, including playing audio and video files without copying them to the phone memory. On my PC, the Sony device mounts like any other flash drive. I would give this 5 stars if it was $30 (and if it came with better instructions), but the $45 price seems high for what is essentially a flash drive with a micro-USB port. You can get the same functionality (in a larger form factor) by using a regular flash drive and an OTG cable (sold here on Amazon for less than $2).

EDIT: I'm still happy with this device, but since writing this review, I've noticed that several other companies (SanDisk and others) have come out with similar products (flash drives with both micro and regular USB connectors) and some of them have much faster USB3.0 speeds. Solo Jay 15.6 Inch Leather Laptop Tote, Espresso Update: I am changing my review of the bag from 4 stars to 3. As I've had it for about a year now, I'm actually starting to dislike it. The leather is wearing at the corners and it doesn't have quite enough space for everything I need to carry. And the falling over is driving me insane. Clearly I was blinded by the newness of the bag when I said it wouldn't prevent me from ordering again. It very much would. I'm already looking into a different work bag.

Really happy with this bag. I wanted a professional looking tote that would fit my water bottle, wallet, a book, and a few work essentials like my clipboard/notebook combo. And it had to zip and not have an obnoxious company logo on the front. This bag fits the bill and looks very nice. I've gotten a lot of compliments on it. It does have the company logo on it but it's so small I often don't notice it.

A lot of other reviewers mentioned that the bag falls over frequently, and this is true, so that's why I'm knocking off a star, but if I had to go back and buy this bag again I still would despite knowing about the falling over issue. I just prop it against the wall in my office or a chair if I'm out and about--the little metal feet help prevent the bottom from getting too soiled. And if it does fall over, well, it's zipped up so nothing falls out of it.
text_fidelity_b: Solo Jay 15.6 Inch Leather Laptop Tote, Espresso

It gets a bit warm during heavy transfer activity, but not enough to be a problem. The only reason I didn’t give 5 stars is because it is fairly slow for large files. My intent was to replace my Sangean 909 ATS which has been showing signs of not being as sensitive to DX and SW-SSB stations. After trying .....with the included antenna and several add on antennas i was disappointed to find that this radio was less useful in listening to SW-SSB than the Sangean which has LOTS OF HOURS ON IT.
